cover.title: 5 niche things that will make you annoyingly good at eu accessibility law

inner.title: the €2m escape hatch
inner.body: e-commerce is covered since 28 june 2025 unless you're a microenterprise: under 10 staff and €2m turnover or balance sheet. outgrow either and you're in.

inner.title: borders won't save you
inner.body: law firm cms notes companies outside the eu may fall under the eaa if they serve eu consumers. your offshore entity is not a shield.

inner.title: your terms must say it
inner.body: annex v says services must explain how they meet accessibility requirements in their terms or equivalent. a missing statement is the easiest gap to spot.

inner.title: wcag is just a third
inner.body: luxembourg's accessibility portal says wcag covers about 36% of applicable en 301 549 criteria. a clean wcag audit still leaves most of it untested.

inner.title: 71% wasn't enough
inner.body: on 4 june 2026 a caen court ordered carrefour to make its site and app fully accessible within six months. it rejected 71% compliance.

closer.HEADLINE:
accessibility is binary,
not a percentage.
closer.SUBLINE: europe audits your checkout, not your intent
closer.TONIGHT: run a screen reader through checkout
